name: Claude syndrome (dorsal midbrain tegmentum)
presentation: A patient develops a third nerve palsy on one side and, on the opposite side, an ataxic arm and leg with dysmetria and an intention tremor, without weakness. The combination of an ipsilateral oculomotor palsy and contralateral cerebellar signs places the lesion in the midbrain tegmentum, where the third nerve fascicles cross the superior cerebellar peduncle decussation and the red nucleus.

deficits.sign: Third nerve palsy, often with pupil involvement
Limb ataxia, dysmetria and intention tremor

reasoning: The dentate nucleus sends its output through the superior cerebellar peduncle, which decussates in the caudal midbrain and then ends in or passes through the red nucleus of the opposite side on its way to the thalamus. A lesion of the paramedian midbrain tegmentum at the level of the red nucleus therefore interrupts cerebellar outflow that has already crossed, and since that outflow, after relaying in the thalamus and motor cortex, would have crossed again through the corticospinal tract to reach the limbs on the side of the original cerebellar hemisphere, the ataxia appears on the side opposite the midbrain lesion. The oculomotor fascicles run through the same region on their way from the nucleus to the interpeduncular fossa and are lost on the side of the lesion, since the nerve is the final ipsilateral motor pathway. The crus cerebri lies ventral to the lesion and is spared, so there is no hemiplegia, which separates Claude from Weber; involvement of the red nucleus itself with rubral tremor and some weakness makes it Benedikt. The supplying vessels are the paramedian perforators from the top of the basilar and the proximal posterior cerebral artery.

imagingFindings.finding: Small area of restricted diffusion in the paramedian midbrain tegmentum at the level of the red nucleus.
Small hyperdense tegmental hemorrhage; check for cavernoma on MRI.

commonCauses: Perforator infarct from the posterior cerebral or basilar artery

mimics.name: Benedikt syndrome
mimics.howToDistinguish: Adds contralateral tremor and involuntary movements from the red nucleus

mimics.name: Cerebellar infarct with a separate third nerve palsy
mimics.howToDistinguish: Ataxia would be ipsilateral to the cerebellar lesion
